TASK1_is_the_unclaimed_2425_ETH_the_same.repointing_mechanism: In the FoMo3D/PlayerBook design LW forks: the pID<->address link is set on first interaction (determinePID: plyr_[pID].addr = msg.sender). To bind a NEW address to an EXISTING pID you use PlayerBook addMeToGame / addMeToAllGames / registerNameX*, ALL of which require pIDxAddr_[msg.sender] != 0 - i.e. you must already control an address on that pID. NO admin override, NO permissionless 'claim this pID'. => repointing is PERMISSIONED (only the pID owner / holder of their key). It CAN be used defensively (a worried owner with their 2018 key binds a fresh secure address and withdraws from it first) but still needs the old key and is a race. Not observed happening in this operation - the drain just calls withdraw() straight from the compromised 2018 EOAs; dead-proxy vaults have no rescue path for anyone.
TASK1_is_the_unclaimed_2425_ETH_the_same.answer_ORIGINAL_2026-09-07_spot_check: MOSTLY NO. TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_A.what_that_implies_about_the_cause: The 11-16 shared wallets = fleet wallets that ALSO had independently-weak/leaked keys, so BOTH a general weak-key hunter (0xA707) and the fleet-keystore holder (our operation) could drain them; 0xA707 got there ~3 days earlier. It IS consistent with the fleet's 2018 wallet generator being weak (some subset independently crackable). 0xA707 is an unrelated opportunist. (This does NOT by itself resolve consolidation-vs-theft - see TASK2, now ~50/50.)
TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_A.why_not_trivially_weak_keys: 40/40 sampled LW fleet members had NO outgoing tx in 2020-2025 (2 exceptions). The long-running 'blockchain bandit' / ISE-Ethercombing sweepers have continuously drained trivially-guessable keys (small integers, common brainwallets) since 2016. These survived 8 years untouched => the keys are NOT in that trivially-weak class. They resisted casual sweeping but fell to a dedicated 2025-26 effort => a MODERATELY weak RNG (~tens of bits of real entropy) or a keystore/seed leak that only surfaced/was worth exploiting in 2025-26.
most_likely_specific_scenarios_for_the_L: (A) FARMING-BOT KEY STORE. The 2018 FoMo3D-clone farming operations needed thousands of funded hot wallets; the bot software held those keys in bulk (a keystore file / DB / config, or derived from one master seed). That store leaked / was sold and is now circulating among multiple drainers. Fits: purpose-made wallets, shared bankrolls, dormant since farming stopped, >1 actor now holding them.

(B) WEAK RNG IN THE 2018 TOOLING OR THE LASTWINNER APP. If the bot wallet generator (or the app's client-side key-gen) seeded a PRNG with low entropy (Date.now(), a counter, PID, JS Math.random()), the real keyspace could be ~32-52 bits - too big for 2016-era casual sweeping, brute-forceable with 2025-26 GPU/cloud once someone realised a whole cohort shared the flaw. Canonical precedent: the Profanity vanity-address tool (32-bit seed, fully brute-forced in the 2022 Wintermute/1inch loss). Independently discoverable => explains multiple simultaneous drainers. ASSESSED 2026-09-09 (scratch/app_history_findings.md 6b): the archived 2018 LW guide confirms an on-device BIP39 'create wallet' flow (+ a PIN 'for payment verification', probably signing auth not a seed passphrase) - the right surface for this vector. 'LW copied FoMo3D's keygen' is a broken inference (FoMo3D shipped no wallet - SECBIT's weak keys were Trust Wallet's iOS build). But the timeline does NOT clear LW: dependency pins mean an upstream fix only reaches an app when it rebuilds, and SECBIT's fix chain was still vulnerable at LW's 2018-08-06 launch (trezor-crypto-ios 0.0.7 = 2018-07-16, but trust-core 0.1.2 / trust-keystore 0.4.3 = 2018-08-08, trust-wallet-ios = 2018-08-21). LW's app was v1.0.0, its site 404'd by 2018-10-12, no evidence of any update => one never-patched build minted BOTH the Aug and Nov 2018 fleet waves, which is why the drainer can hold the complete fleet as one roster. Still unconfirmed that LW's app used trust-core / trezor-crypto / a copied srand(time()) snippet - needs the binary. FEASIBILITY favours this vector: the fleet's key-gen window is ~2 wk (Aug) + ~1 mo (Nov) 2018 ~= 3.8M one-second timestamps; a SECBIT-style regeneration over it is minutes of compute and yields the COMPLETE fleet in one pass - matching the observed 'one entity, full 44k roster, uniform drain'. 0xA707's 11-16 independent fleet hits, spread across the launch fortnight, imply a real fraction of the fleet has keys in a regenerable class (counter: TRM publicly tied 0xA707 to the 2022 LastPass breach = credential theft, not RNG). STRONG NEW EVIDENCE 2026-09-09 (app_history_findings.md 6b.1): the LW app auto-generates the account name as [A-Za-z]{15} + a 13-digit Date.now() MILLISECOND timestamp and registers it on-chain via registerNameXID - 99/99 sampled names match exactly, and the embedded ms precedes the on-chain tx by a median 22s. So the wallet-creation millisecond is PUBLIC in calldata for the ~38% of the fleet that registered a name (~13k wallets): a key regeneration no longer needs to bound the seed, the name pins it to ~1000 ms. The 15-char prefix is a public sample of the app's client-side RNG stream. Date.now()+[A-Za-z] strings => the generator is JAVASCRIPT (RN/Cordova/webview), so the precedent is a weak JS Math.random()/Date-seeded wallet RNG, not only the trezor-crypto C bug. Same pull: 95% of fleet wallets' first LW tx is their nonce-0 tx (app-minted, not imported); gas limit 800000 on 97% (app-hardcoded, scripted); 254/259 distinct referrer codes (broad flat pyramid, affCode never 0); funding NOT relayer-sponsored (67% straight from the 6 HTX/BW hot wallets). Still NOT proven that the mnemonic entropy came from the same weak call - but the 'can't pin the timestamp' obstacle is gone and there's a public RNG readout to test. CENSUS 2026-09-09 (app_history_findings.md 6b.1b, 1,600 drained vs 1,600 undrained LW players): the WHOLE LW playerbase is app-minted, and the drained set is a slightly PURER cut of it. Shared signals ~equal (app auto-name ~40%/38% of callers; human-chosen name 0 of 1311 drained / 1 of 1561 undrained). BUT the imported-wallet tail differs ~6x: genuine pre-deploy/external wallets = 0.9% of drained callers vs 5.8% of undrained; nonce-0 first-LW-tx 94.2% vs 87.9%. => the drainer's reach ~= exactly the app keyspace; it barely touched the ~6% who played with their own MetaMask/imToken wallet. A MODEST lean toward weak-RNG regeneration (an attacker who regenerated the app keyspace cannot reach external keys); NOT proof (a keystore leak could also miss non-custodied imports). Blast radius if weak: the full ~63k+ app userbase, not just the drained 44k (~19k undrained left = empty). App-pattern Date.now() span 2018-08-06 14:38 UTC -> mid-Nov 2018, genuine ms resolution. REGENERATION PoC 2026-09-09 (local, not published): NEGATIVE across 30 drained registerNameXID wallets. (A) native srand(time())+rand() - 6 rand() models (MSVC/POSIX/Apple64+32/MINSTD/glibc-TYPE3), +/-120s window + uint32/64 casts, entropy->{raw|keccak|BIP32seed|BIP39-12|BIP39-24} x {m/44'/60'/0'/0/0, .../0}: 0 hits. (B) prefix seed-lock - 9 PRNGs (+ 9301-LCG/mulberry32/sfc32/MT19937), 6 char-maps, +/-1800s on second AND ms: 0 streams reproduce the 15-char name prefix on any target. => the easily-bruteable weak-RNG forms are RULED OUT (name != simple clock-seeded PRNG; key != srand(time())+rand()). Left: (1) auto-seeded Math.random() (V8 xorshift128+/JSC) needing SMT state-recovery from the 15 quantised prefix chars - real project, uncertain; (2) model gaps (glibc warmup, alphabet order, PIN-as-BIP39-passphrase, exotic path); (3) the KEY used a real CSPRNG and only the NAME is weak, so keys are NOT derivable and the vector is a keystore/backend leak - this negative tilts slightly toward (3)/scenario (A). Pipeline verified vs Trezor abandon..about + a synthetic wallet; drop in the real algo (binary, or one ground-truth seed phrase) and the whole name corpus falls. BLOCKED on the app binary: OSS bucket now NoSuchBucket; Wayback only has 2020 parking-page captures of lastwinner_1.0.0.apk / lw.js.

(C) SHARED HD SEED / ONE KEYSTORE FILE. One BIP-39 mnemonic (or one bulk keystore) -> the whole fleet. Fits the ~44% coToken-pool subset and the uniform 2026 roster-style drain; but the fleet is NOT proven to be one operation (its funding is via a shared exchange, ~56% are outside the coToken pool).

(D) 3rd-PARTY CUSTODIAL / BACKEND LEAK (the LastWinner app's server, or a shared wallet service). Matches Jeff Schvey's read; matches 'app that lowered the barrier to entry'. Best fit for the WIDER April-2026 wave / the 0xA707 victims that are NOT LastWinner wallets.

Official guide allowed create OR import (mnemonic/PK) + a wallet PIN, but 2018 Chinese reviews (Jiemian/Zhihu) say the create-new flow did NOT show / back up / export the private key => effectively CUSTODIAL, team-held keys. On-device (weak RNG) vs server-side generation NOT established - needs the binary or the 2018 front-end JS bundles (lastwinner.me is dead; Wayback CDX has snapshots; commands in the findings file). DIRECT PRECEDENT for scenario (B): SECBIT 'Trust Wallet's Fomo3D Summer' (2024) - Trust Wallet's 2018 iOS build seeded its RNG with srand((unsigned)time(NULL)), producing same-second wallet collisions; >2,100 ETH later drained, and many of those wallets had been created specifically to play FoMo3D. A LastWinner app with the same class of bug would produce exactly this cohort.
TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_A.leaning: (A) or (B). Multi-actor simultaneity most specifically fits (B) weak RNG (independently reproducible) or (A) a leaked store traded to several parties. The custodial nature of the app's create-new flow (D) + the SECBIT Trust Wallet precedent strengthen (B): a team-controlled, on-device-generated keyset with a time-seeded RNG. Confirmation needs the 2018 app binary / its front-end JS, or a researcher publishing the cracked-key structure.

TASK2_theft_vs_legitimate_consolidation.verdict: GENUINELY UNRESOLVED, ~50/50. (Earlier drafts of this file swung between 'THEFT strongly-supported' and '~70/30 consolidation'. Both over-stated. The ~70/30 consolidation lean rested largely on a supposed pre-drain 'wind-down' that turned out to be HTX exchange housekeeping - retracted. See notes_on_interpretation.)
for_theft / compromise: Publicly reported as an attack (WazzCrypto/Specter 2026-04-30, 7+ outlets); Etherscan 'Fake_Phishing2831105' label on a related address.
Part of a broader April-2026 wave of dormant-wallet drains attributed to weak/leaked legacy keys.
At least one affected user publicly treated a drained wallet as their own.
ETH moved directly out of EOAs (no contract exploit) => the operator holds the keys, however obtained.
for_consolidation / rightful holder: One entity holds an ORGANISED set of ~44,000 keys and works it as a roster (incl. 8,868 zero-balance withdraw() calls) - looks like managing a known list, not opportunistic scraping.
PARKS rather than dumps: ~2,907 ETH unmoved in 0xe4a219fbed for 40+ days; only ~325 ETH known bridged out (by the SEPARATE 0xA707 actor).

The victim set is overwhelmingly a 2018 LastWinner farming cohort - leftover bot-operation bankroll (the fleet LOST ~38% at the game; the residual ETH is unspent working capital, not winnings - see TASK_how_profitable_was_the_2018_farming_for_the_fleet), not innocent retail savings; a ~44% subset used a shared pool (coToken).
The separate 0xA707 drainer, which DID cash out fast to BTC/XMR, shares only ~11-16 keys - i.e. our operation is not just 'another weak-key sweeper'.
TASK2_theft_vs_legitimate_consolidation.what_would_decide_it: The compromise vector (open question #1). A reproducible weak RNG that anyone can exploit => leans theft/opportunism. A single keystore/seed that only the fleet operator(s) ever held => leans consolidation. Also: if the parked ETH (0xe4a219fbed etc.) is bridged to a mixer / fresh exchange deposit => more theft-like; if redeployed or held => more owner-like.
TASK2_theft_vs_legitimate_consolidation.most_probable_vector: Weak / predictable private-key generation in the 2018 farming tooling and/or the LastWinner app (cf. SECBIT 'Trust Wallet's Fomo3D Summer', srand(time(NULL))). Unconfirmed. This is a concentrated pocket within a broader April-2026 dormant-wallet key-compromise wave - the LastWinner tie is this repo's contribution.

TASK_characterise_the_non_lastwinner_sub.question: Some drained wallets apparently never touched the LastWinner contract. Are they linked to the LastWinner fleet, or an independent subset that just happened to be swept?
TASK_characterise_the_non_lastwinner_sub.population: The genuine non-participant set = touched_lastwinner=='unknown' AND drained_via=='looseETH' (no withdraw()) in drained_eoas.csv = 7,654 addresses. findings.they_really_did_not_play_the_game: 2/220 (~1%) ever sent a tx to OR received a payout from the LastWinner contract across full history (vs 128/130 in the control). 0/220 ever touched the original FoMo3D-long (same as control) - so this is not generic 2018-gambling-wallet key exposure, it is LastWinner-ecosystem-specific.
findings.same_creation_windows: 88% first-funded in 2018, concentrated in the two known fleet waves - 75/220 in Aug 2018, 83/220 in Nov 2018. Control: 100% in 2018, almost all Aug.
findings.same_pooling_structure_at_the_same_rate: 46% of the non-participant sample hit >=1 shared 2018-19 pool / batch-distributor / token contract, vs 52% of the control - and the SAME contracts dominate both: coToken pool 0x03cb0021 (40% of non-LW vs 37% of control), its distributor 0x105631c6 (5,844 senders, alive only 29-30 Nov 2018), plus 0xae9b8e05 / 0x4f5f88bbaf / 0x95428ac0 (each 3,000-4,500 senders, each alive 2-6 days, Dec 2018 - Mar 2019) and a 'Fus'/'FusChain' token (0x573aaaa8 / 0xade2fc8d). For 77/220 the FIRST outbound action is a deposit to coToken.
findings.shared_funding_infra: 15% first-funded directly by one of the six HTX/BW hot wallets (vs 68% of the control - lower, because the non-participant wing sits one hop further back). The recurring non-CEX funders (0xeec606a66e, 0xf775a9a0ad, 0xb2a48f542d, 0x6958c3fde1, 0x75a83599de, 0x8d9cc1d96c) are large 2017-18 fan-out wallets (6,000-6,700 distinct recipients each); at least two of them fund BOTH the non-participant and the confirmed-player samples.
findings.same_2026_drain: 100% of the non-participant sample was swept in 2026 to a known LastWinner-drain collector (july 0xa279ffef / aug24 0x8d7c20e3 / burst-2 0x5723168b) - identical infrastructure and timing to the confirmed players. This is the strongest single link: one keyholder worked both wings as one roster.
findings.what_they_are: ~46% = the pooled-betting wing: created in-wave, deposited to coToken / a batch contract, the pool (or a proxy) played LastWinner, so the EOA never appears as a caller and never had a vault. ~54% = plain reserve / staging wallets: funded in-wave from the same infra, 1-4 throwaway txs, then dormant until the 2026 sweep.

caveats: Sample-based (220 of 7,654). The ~1% direct-play rate has a wide CI but is unambiguously far below the earlier ~62% claim.
'Hit a shared pool contract' is a coordination signal, not proof of one operator; ~54% of the sample hit none and are only tied in by creation window + funding route + the 2026 drain.

The 2 apparent players in the non-LW sample are just mislabels (real players the mid-Sep-2018 caller scan missed), consistent with touched_lastwinner=='unknown' meaning 'not confirmed', not 'confirmed absent'.

TASK_how_profitable_was_the_2018_farming.question: How profitable was the LastWinner operation for the drained addresses themselves?
TASK_how_profitable_was_the_2018_farming.method: Per-wallet cash P&L from full history (Alchemy alchemy_getAssetTransfers): buys = ETH sent to the LastWinner contract, returns = ETH received from it (withdraw() payouts / pot / affiliate, lifetime). Sample: 280 random touched_lastwinner=='yes' + 160 random non-LW/coToken-wing wallets (seed 7). Analysis scripts run locally (not published). Extrapolations x126.9 (35,527 confirmed players) and x47.8 (7,654 non-LW wing) are rough - high per-wallet variance.
TASK_how_profitable_was_the_2018_farming.headline: At the game itself the fleet LOST money - heavily. The confirmed-player wallets put ~49,000 ETH into the LastWinner contract over their life and got ~30,800 ETH back = ~-18,500 ETH net, a ~62% return on ETH wagered (-38%). 89% of sampled wallets are net-negative; only 11% came out ahead. Median wallet -0.29 ETH. Sampled winners totalled +54 ETH against losers' -200 ETH. Gas (270k+ tx during the Aug-2018 congestion they caused) adds a further est. 1,000-3,000 ETH of loss on top.
TASK_how_profitable_was_the_2018_farming.the_residual_is_leftover_bankroll_not_wi: What survived to 2026 in these wallets - the ~4,000-4,550 ETH the drainer is now sweeping (loose EOA ETH + small unclaimed vaults; our sample extrapolates to ~4,000, matching the repo headline ~4,550) - is NOT accumulated game profit. It is unspent working capital that was funded into the wallets and never fully cycled through the contract, plus a thin layer of un-withdrawn dividends. The vaults left for the 2026 drainer to withdraw() were tiny (sample: ~10 ETH across 280 players -> ~1,300 ETH fleet-wide, i.e. most of the 1,545 ETH burst total came from the wider 25,328-caller set, and per wallet it is dust).
TASK_how_profitable_was_the_2018_farming.non_lw_wing: The non-LW / coToken wing barely touched the game (~0 ETH wagered). Their exposure was via the coToken pool - small amounts, roughly break-even to slightly positive in the sample, but coToken only ever held ~187 ETH total so the absolute figure is low (order tens-to-low-hundreds of ETH). The ~824 ETH the drainer takes from this wing is again leftover seed capital sitting idle since 2018.
two_readings: (A) WASH-TRADING COST CENTRE. If this fleet is (mostly) the operator's own volume-faking bots - the repo's leading read, and the 2018 press's 'operator pre-loaded ETH to run bot transactions' claim - then the ~18,500 ETH 'loss' is not lost to an outside party: it flowed into the dev fee, the airdrop/dividend pools and the pot, much of which the operator or allied early wallets also controlled. The fleet is a manufacturing expense; the operation's true P&L sits at the operator/contract level, which this repo has never been able to measure (deployer 0xeae69cad is a throwaway; the ~7,754 ETH pot winner was never traced).

(B) GENUINE LOSSES. If the fleet is independent farmers / retail marks, then the ~18,500 ETH is a real transfer to (i) the ~2-5% dev fee, (ii) earlier / larger keyholders' dividends, (iii) the outside airdrop-farming group BAPT-LW20 (Kraken-funded, ~1,000 proxy contracts, took ~12,948 ETH = airdrop pool + grand prize per AnChain - a SEPARATE group from this Huobi-funded fleet), (iv) whoever won the pot.
TASK_how_profitable_was_the_2018_farming.bottom_line: For the addresses themselves the operation was value-destroying: ~49k ETH wagered, ~31k ETH returned, and the ~4-4.5k ETH that outlived 2018 is being taken in 2026 by whoever holds the keys - not by the original farmer. The only party with a clean realised gain tied to these wallets is the 2026 drainer (~4,000-4,550 ETH, minus trivial gas).
caveats: 'buys' captures external ETH into the contract; reLoadXid (buying more keys out of the vault) is not a cash outlay and is intentionally excluded - cash-in vs cash-out is still correct.
Sampling error is real: aggregate net could plausibly be -25% to -50%. But '89% of wallets underwater / winners +54 vs losers -200' is not near the line.

'external ETH into the wallets' (~119k ETH extrapolated) is inflated by exchange hot-wallet round-trips and non-fleet intermediaries - do NOT read it as capital deployed. The cleaner size-of-operation number is the ~49k ETH actually wagered.
This measures wallet-level cash flow, not the operator's books. Reading (A) vs (B) is unresolved (same open question as consolidation-vs-theft / who ran the fleet).

the_2018_cast.1_game_operator: deployer 0xeae69cADEB04E66767bD69f52e0fFFc28E37d799 = a DISPOSABLE throwaway: only 23 txs ever, funded with just 3 ETH (from 0x8cc33572319f), deployed + did initial addGame()/activate()/atInversebrah() admin, then near-dead. the_2018_cast.3_coToken_pool: 0x03cb0021 - a small ETH deposit/withdraw POOLING contract, name()='coToken', ~187 ETH, 552 depositors, active ONLY Nov 4-29 2018. the_2018_cast.note: So the 2,425 ETH still in the contract ~= the vaults of ~1,000 addresses that were contracts and self-destructed in Aug 2018 (no code, no key, permanently stuck) + genuinely abandoned wallets. The drain only ever touched LIVE 2018 EOAs.
the_2018_cast.does_the_2018_200k-ETH_bot-funding_claim: PARTIALLY, and weaker after the HTX correction. SUBSTANCE: there was a large 2018 LastWinner farming set of ~44k wallets, funded via Huobi/HTX withdrawals, playing from launch - consistent with the 2018 Chinese reports of manufactured volume. But we have NOT identified a single 'bankroll' entity (the wallets we thought were that are exchange hot wallets), so 'professionally bankrolled by one operation' is now unproven. NUMBER: '200,000 ETH' is a soft 2018 estimate, not verified here - our sample puts ETH actually wagered through the contract by the drained fleet at ~49k ETH (order of magnitude below the 200k headline; the two need not measure the same thing). ECONOMICS: the fleet lost ~38% at the game (~49k ETH in, ~31k ETH back; see TASK_how_profitable_was_the_2018_farming_for_the_fleet) - which fits 'wash-trading bots bleeding the house edge' as much as 'losing gamblers'. The punchline stands: that 2018 farming set is what is being drained in 2026.
